Curlimp 0.4.0 corrects CA override precedence, HTTP 304 file preservation, early profile validation, ordered stdin readers, HEAD/include option order, and JSON stdout conflicts. It has 38 browser profiles with Chrome 150 still the default.

## Compatibility change

`okhttp4_android` and its native `okhttp4` alias have been removed because the preset's default headers were inconsistent with the advertised client. Both now fail before response or header files are opened. Use `curlimp --list-profiles` to choose a supported preset.

## Fixes and native inputs

- Explicit `--cacert` or `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` suppresses `SSL_CERT_DIR`; otherwise `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` can both apply. A successful HTTP 304 with no selected bytes no longer truncates an existing `-o` file.
- Stdin sources are read in option order, including superseded `-w @-` readers. `-I` enables HEAD and header selection; a later `--no-include` keeps HEAD while omitting selected headers, including in exports.
- `--json-output -c -` fails early so stdout contains only a JSON document. TXT and JSON-file exports still permit an explicitly requested stdout cookie jar. File exports themselves do not print response bytes to stdout.
- Supported command-line user and proxy credentials are masked in process arguments after startup on shipped Linux and macOS builds. This does not clear shell history or prevent every startup race. Upload bodies remain buffered; a redundant resolved copy is released before transfer.
- zlib is updated to 1.3.2. nghttp2 remains 1.63.0 for legacy priorities and includes the upstream CVE-2026-27135 stop-reading fix as a backport. This release does not claim an exploit was demonstrated against Curlimp.

## Update Docker

```sh
docker pull juanfontes/curlimp
docker run --rm juanfontes/curlimp -sS -I https://httpbin.org/status/200
docker run --rm juanfontes/curlimp:0.4.0 firefox147 --json-output -sS -i https://httpbin.org/status/418
```

The untagged image follows Docker `latest` after a newer stable release is promoted; Docker may otherwise use a cached local image. The `0.4.0` tag is a fixed release selection. Linux amd64 and arm64 are the image platforms. The root Dockerfile selects that versioned runtime by default; `RUNTIME_IMAGE` can select a digest.

## Native downloads and validation

Download the matching Linux amd64/arm64 or experimental macOS Apple Silicon archive with `SHA256SUMS` from this release. Verify the archive checksum, extract it, and keep the full bundle together. Run `./curlimp --version`. The macOS bundle is signed ad hoc and not notarized; it targets macOS 13.0, while CI runs on macOS 15. There are no native Windows or Intel Mac downloads. See the [installation guide](https://juanfontes.github.io/curlimp/docs/installation/) for commands.

Publication requires exact-source CI for all three native targets, including extracted bundles and final Linux container DNS/HTTPS plus mounted nonroot JSON export. Local focused checks cover the behavior fixes, macOS source build, and Linux arm64 runtime; this text does not claim completed final cross-platform CI. Dependency reporting is read-only and limited to its documented official feeds. Browser fingerprint equivalence and HTTP/3 browser fidelity remain unverified.
